title: Man dead in Niverville after police shooting
article: An officer-involved shooting left one person dead, one in custody and one on the run Wednesday and an RCMP f orensic unit investigating at a Niverville gas station where a body and damaged pickup truck were located.

The incident was related to a manhunt that took place in Saskatchewan on Wednesday, as RCMP from that province said they were searching for a suspect vehicle believed to be travelling westbound on Highway 22, possibly to the Fort Qu'Appelle area and said residents in the area should be cautious.

Saskatchewan RCMP said the suspect fled from the scene of an officer-involved shooting in Niverville, a town south of Winnipeg. Police later confirmed the suspect was arrested in Saskatchewan on Wednesday afternoon, and is now in custody.
Around 11 a.m. Wednesday morning, the Manitoba RCMP Forensics unit and other officers were investigating in the Shell and Tim Horton's lot in Niverville along Highway 311.
Around noon both the body and the vehicle were removed from the scene.

Winnipeg police said that around 12:40 a.m. Wednesday morning they received information through RCMP regarding a Black Ford 350 reported stolen from a rural Manitoba municipality southwest of Winnipeg.
They were also told the vehicle was occupied by several potentially armed individuals involved in prior criminal activity and was making its way to Winnipeg.
Around 12:50 a.m., an officer saw the stolen vehicle near Ness Avenue and Linwood Street in Winnipeg, and police said a lengthy follow ensued, lasting approximately one hour.
Officers said they drove into a parking lot in Otterburne where a cruiser was rammed by the stolen vehicle and shots were fired by officers before the suspects fled.

The vehicle, which was also being monitored by a police helicopter, later pulled into a parking lot in Niverville and officers saw the driver exit the stolen vehicle, enter another vehicle, and flee the area. An adult female passenger attempted to flee on foot but was apprehended and arrested.
Police said a third suspect was found in the truck suffering from a gunshot wound and officers provided emergency care, but he succumbed to his injuries.
The Independent Investigation Unit of Manitoba (IIU) said they have now assumed responsibility for the investigation with assistance from RCMP.
"As this matter involves a fatality, the IIU will request the Manitoba Police Commission appoint a civilian monitor," IIU said in a media release.
"Witnesses or individuals who have information or video footage that may assist the investigation are asked to contact the IIU toll-free at 1-844-667-6060."
In a statement, Niverville Mayor Myron Dyck thanked police for their efforts on Wednesday morning to contain the situation.
"We are thankful for the police and their service to our community," Dyck said. "They have a tough job to do, and do it well."
Rachelle Baker has lived in Niverville for nine years, and said the news of the incident sent a shock through the town.

"The first thing that many of us do in the morning is reach for our telephones and immediately we were hit with the news," Baker said. "We're a small town and not a lot of things like this happen, so this has really rocked people."
Baker has two kids who go to schools in the area, and said she was notified schools in the town were in lockdown on Wednesday morning.

"We got notifications this morning about kids being let into the school immediately as they arrived, and the ones that go home for lunch will have to be picked up and taken back to the schools," she said.

She added there was a sense of unease in the community because of news Wednesday morning that a suspect was still on the loose, and before hearing that the suspect had fled west, and was likely no longer in the area.
"It was scary because no one really knew this morning what was happening, and it's one of those things where you see the crime scene and you realize this is real and it's surreal," Baker said.
"Seeing a crime scene, it doesn't happen here."
